implementation_notes: @dynamicMemberLookup and @dynamicCallable (SE-0195, SE-0216) are compile-time sugar that turns x.anything into a subscript and x(...) into dynamicallyCall, and the proposals name dynamic proxy objects and language interop as their justification. The classic runtime proxy cannot exist in pure Swift, because Swift types are fixed at compile time; these attributes give the call-site ergonomics of a proxy object without fabricating a type, so they are the honest default for pure-Swift code.
pitfalls: @dynamicMemberLookup disables member checking: a typo becomes a dynamic lookup that compiles and fails at run time, and no protocol conformance is implied.
The dynamic members are not real properties, so key paths, Codable synthesis and generic constraints over protocols do not see them.
Compile-time sugar does not make the object a proxy for a concrete type: callers still hold JSValue, not the target's static type.

variants.name: Objective-C runtime message forwarding (NSProxy)
variants.implementation_notes: Real runtime forwarding exists only through the Objective-C runtime that Swift can use for @objc-visible classes: subclass NSProxy (or NSObject) and implement forwardingTarget(for:) for cheap hand-off, or methodSignature(for:) plus forwardInvocation(_:) for full forwarding, and override responds(to:)/conforms(to:) so callers believe the proxy. It is the only way to stand in for a class whose methods are not declared in Swift, but it cannot stand in for Swift structs, enums or protocol existentials of Swift types - dynamic casts then disagree about the class (reported on swift-dev).
pitfalls: Swift-only types cannot be proxied this way: an NSProxy stand-in for a Swift class makes dynamic casts and KVO disagree with the runtime, which crashes rather than degrades.
Forgetting to override responds(to:)/conforms(to:) makes Cocoa frameworks decide the proxy cannot handle the message and never send it.
Objective-C message forwarding is the slow path: every forwarded call allocates an NSInvocation unless forwardingTarget(for:) short-circuits it.
